primary.scope: Separate descriptive local comparison; compilation/setup excluded; not a paired improvement gate or whole-runtime parity proof.
primary.experimental_unit: Median of two independent process medians; mean of two independent process means. Original pooled42 summaries retained separately.

boundaries.scriptw: Source/native compilation, fresh Store/linker and module instantiation precede execution. main executes ProgramInitialize, R literal-cache initialization, fresh Realm setup, source and completion/output handling inside execution_ns.
boundaries.v8: Source vm.Script compilation and vm.createContext are outside execution_ns. script.runInContext is timed in a fresh context. Context creation is separately recorded; fresh-Realm setup is therefore not identically inside both runtimes execution metrics.
boundaries.scriptc: The JS frontend/Zig compilation is a separate process. WASI host module compilation, fresh Store and instantiation are outside execution_ns; _start and output-buffer extraction are timed.
boundaries.rss: Post-execution process endpoints, not peak/live workload heap, and frontend memory is separate for Scriptc. No comparative live-allocation/RSS efficiency claim follows.
boundaries.meaning: These retain the established local execution boundaries. They are not an equal-cost end-to-end fresh-Realm benchmark, conformance result or updated published performance chart.

close_to_sorted.interpretation: Candidate is0.585354% slower by the primary median. Round0 candidate median is slower, round1 faster. Candidate means are slower in both rounds. This close descriptive result does not establish equality or parity; do not round582.7845us and579.393us into a claimed tie.

unchanged_objects_caution.interpretation: Its P bytes and linked R are unchanged between Scriptw baseline/candidate. The reference baseline/candidate timing difference is not an optimization effect established by this batch. Its Scriptc win is median-only; candidate mean is about1.11% slower.

remaining_cost_assessment.observed_workload_cluster: Primary Scriptw medians for exact-sum numeric10k/50k and the three optimized joins are approximately254–279us. This is a measured whole-workload cluster; no pure Realm/bootstrap cost or component fraction was isolated.

actual_numeric_code.scriptw_observation: Guarded exact-sum path converts the initial integer seed, adds i64 constant3749975000, converts back to f64 and publishes counter50000. Generic/chunked fallback remains.
actual_numeric_code.scriptc_observation: Actual Wasm retains a five-step unrolled sequence of f64 multiply/add terms, advances an i64 counter by5, and branches until50000.
actual_numeric_code.inference: Scriptw already removes the arithmetic trip count on this admitted source yet is slower overall than Scriptc(254.405us vs154.945us primary medians). Investigate work outside the source arithmetic loop; this does not assign the difference specifically to Realm initialization.

actual_dense_code.observation: One preheader index conversion followed by four typed array.get and original ordered f64 arithmetic/update operations per integer-tested chunk, then an integer scalar tail. Array construction, comparator sort and printing remain outside this read-only checksum region.

actual_join_code.observation: After the bounded String/native-method preflight, the1024-iteration fast loop adds a captured numeric length without repeated join calls or result String construction. The scalar additions and source array/printing remain.

remaining_cost_assessment.larger_workloads: The larger join/objects controls have unchanged P code. Their remaining work includes array/object construction, string operations and output. Existing packed push already bypasses argument vectors for one to three saved operands; a future construction region must remove repeated lookup/guards/growth under real prototype/write proofs, not rediscover that fast path.
future_priorities_not_implemented: Profile actual first-entry work around ProgramInitialize/Realm installation and output before changing R; preserve setup/entry boundaries and canonical per-Realm identities.
Evaluate a distinct bounded array-construction region with guards for native push, writable/extensible storage, indexed-prototype hazards and zero-trip behavior.
For object-heavy loops, separately measure the previously reviewed compact-property-path preflight against tiny/zero-trip controls; do not infer its benefit from unchanged objects reference timings.
Canonical R String prehashing and immutable key-wrapper sharing are source-supported future leads, not measured explanations of the current gap.

references.note: Separate from paired improvement cohorts. Pooled42-sample summaries remain archived; primary comparisons aggregate independent processes. RSS is process endpoint, not peak or live JS heap. No causal unchanged-control or universal speedup claim.

codegen_evidence.scope: Actual source-bound emitted Wasm/WAT and Scriptc LLVM; no Scriptw R module dump.

limitations: Global V8/Scriptc time and RSS parity remains open.
Selected 997 pinned Test262 passes are not full Test262 or default/all-feature release acceptance.
Unchanged controls have slower mean outliers in the full17 record; all eight control P programs and both R profiles/native images are byte-identical to baseline.
Local records do not replace older published CI benchmarks/status.
The observed 254–279us workload level does not isolate Realm initialization cost.

evidence.policy: UTF-8 non-executable records only; no Wasm/native binaries, caches or toolchains. Source-bound program WAT/LLVM included.
